text: The 'March of Millions' demonstration on 6 May 2012 was held to protest against the allegedly rigged presidential elections.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The 'March of Millions' demonstration on 6 May 2012 had been approved by the Moscow city authorities in the form of a march followed by a meeting at Bolotnaya Square.

text: The approved meeting at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 was supposed to end at 7.30 p.m.

section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: When the marchers arrived at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, it transpired that barriers installed by the police had narrowed the entrance to the meeting venue.

section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: There were numerous clashes between the police and protesters at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police ordered that the meeting at Bolotnaya Square finish early.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 21 February 2014 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found the applicant guilty as charged under Articles 212 § 2 and 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that between 4 p.m. and 8 p.m. on 6 May 2012 at Bolotnaya Square, unidentified persons called those present to move outside the agreed meeting venue and to defy the lawful orders of the police.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that unidentified persons called those present at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 to use violence, which led to mass disorder accompanied by the use of violence against public officials in connection with the performance of their duties and the destruction of property.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that on 6 May 2012 at 5 p.m. at the latest the defendants acquired the criminal intent to participate in mass disorder and to use violence against police officers.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that participants of the acts of mass disorder threw pieces of tarmac, stones, sticks and other objects at the police, which hit them on various parts of their body.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that between 5.05 p.m. and 10 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the applicant shouted insulting slogans and used metal barriers to block the police's movement, thus preventing the arrest of the participants in the acts of mass disorder.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that the applicant, acting intentionally, at least three times threw stones and pieces of tarmac at police officers in a targeted manner during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that the applicant used violence against an unidentified police officer which did not endanger his life or health during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that unidentified participants in the acts of mass disorder tore a protection helmet off an unidentified police officer's head and punched and kicked him several times in the head and body, while the applicant punched this police officer at least once.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that the applicant used violence against Police Officer T. which did not endanger his life or health during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that unidentified participants of the acts of mass disorder intentionally tore off Police Officer T.'s protection helmet, which T. continued to hold in his hands, and punched him in the head and body, whereupon the applicant intentionally grabbed T.'s uniform and snatched the helmet from his hands.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant pleaded not guilty at his criminal trial before the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant testified at his criminal trial that he had decided to attend the public gathering on 6 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant testified at his criminal trial that when leaving the Malyy Kamennyy Bridge he saw a lot of police officers equipped with bullet-proof vests, helmets and truncheons, which filled him with indignation.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant testified at his criminal trial that as nothing was happening on the stage, he decided to return, and when leaving the venue he saw the police officers randomly arresting people while hitting them with truncheons.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant testified at his criminal trial that he was hit in the back three times with a truncheon.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant testified at his criminal trial that when he saw violent acts by the police, he approached the barriers where other protestors were standing and expressed his indignation.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant testified at his criminal trial that when trying to leave the venue, somebody tore off his shirt.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant testified at his criminal trial that at some point he came across Police Officer T., who was not wearing any helmet.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant testified at his criminal trial that when he tried to leave, police officers ran up to him and started to beat him in the head and body, then arrested him and took him to a police vehicle.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant insisted at his criminal trial that he had committed no acts in respect of Police Officer T., had not seen his helmet and had snatched nothing from his hands.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow considered the defendants' arguments that they were protecting somebody from police officers or happened to be victims of the police's use of force as farfetched and aimed at mitigating their responsibility.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant was sentenced to three years and six months' imprisonment.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant's sentence of three years and six months' imprisonment was calculated on the basis of a three-year prison term under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation, partly concurrent with a term of one year under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Article 212 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the organisation of mass disorder, accompanied by violence, riots, arson, destruction of property, the use of firearms, explosives and explosive devices, as well as armed resistance to a public official, shall be punishable by four to ten years' deprivation of liberty.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND PRACTICE

text: Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that participation in the types of mass disorder provided for by Article 212 § 1 shall be punishable by three to eight years' deprivation of liberty.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND PRACTICE

text: Article 212 § 3 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the instigation of mass disorder provided for by Article 212 § 1, or the instigation of participation in such acts, or the instigation of violence against citizens, shall be punishable by a restriction of liberty for up to two years, or community service for up to two years, or deprivation of liberty for the same term.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND PRACTICE

text: Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the use of violence which does not endanger life or health, or the threat to use such violence against a public official or his relatives in connection with the performance of his or her duties, shall be punishable by a fine of up to 200,000 roubles or an equivalent of the convicted person's wages for 18 months, or community service for up to five years, or up to five years' deprivation of liberty.
